program: Frontier wave 4 — famous Mathlib-backed theorems (tractable, high-yield)
principle: Landmark KNOWN theorems that Aristotle can close via Mathlib, to keep the fleet productive while wave-3's hard targets grind. All unconditional known results — verifying famous mathematics, not resolving open problems. AXLE gates.

queue.statement: Fermat's little theorem: for a prime p and any integer a, a^p is congruent to a modulo p. State over ZMod p: for [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] and any x : ZMod p, x ^ p = x. (Use Mathlib's ZMod.pow_card.)
Wilson's theorem: for a prime p, (p-1)! is congruent to -1 modulo p. State: for [Fact (Nat.Prime p)], ((p-1)! : ZMod p) = -1. (Use Mathlib's ZMod.wilsons_lemma.)

Euler's theorem: if a and n are coprime then a^(phi n) is congruent to 1 modulo n. State via ZMod n units, or: for a : ZMod n with IsUnit a, a ^ Nat.totient n = 1. (Use Mathlib's ZMod.pow_totient / ZMod.units_pow_card_sub_one_eq_one area.)
Gauss's law of quadratic reciprocity: for distinct odd primes p q, legendreSym p q * legendreSym q p = (-1)^((p-1)/2 * (q-1)/2). (Use Mathlib's legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity.)

Lagrange's theorem: for a finite group G and a subgroup H, the cardinality of H divides the cardinality of G. State: for [Fintype G] [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) [Fintype H], Fintype.card H divides Fintype.card G. (Use Mathlib's Subgroup.card_subgroup_dvd_card.)

Cauchy's theorem: if a prime p divides the order of a finite group G, then G has an element of order p. State: for [Fintype G] [Group G] and prime p with p divides Fintype.card G, there exists g : G with orderOf g = p. (Use Mathlib's exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card.)

The pigeonhole principle: if f maps a finite type s into a finite type t with card t < card s, then f is not injective (there exist a b in s, a != b, with f a = f b). (Use Mathlib's Fintype.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt.)

The intermediate value theorem: a continuous real function on [a,b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b). State: for a <= b and f continuous on Set.Icc a b, Set.Icc (f a) (f b) is a subset of f '' (Set.Icc a b) (when f a <= f b). (Use Mathlib's intermediate_value_Icc.)

The extreme value theorem: a continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact set attains its maximum. State: for a nonempty compact set s and f continuous on s, there exists x in s with forall y in s, f y <= f x. (Use Mathlib's IsCompact.exists_forall_ge / exists_isMaxOn.)

The fundamental theorem of algebra: every non-constant complex polynomial has a root. State: for p : Polynomial Complex with 0 < p.degree, there exists z : Complex with p.eval z = 0. (Use Mathlib's Complex.exists_root.)

There are infinitely many primes congruent to 3 modulo 4: for every N there exists a prime p with N < p and p % 4 = 3. (A special case provable elementarily / via Mathlib's Nat.setOf_prime infinite results or a direct Euclid-style argument.)
A closed bounded interval of the reals is compact: Set.Icc a b is compact (IsCompact (Set.Icc a b)) for real a b. (Use Mathlib's isCompact_Icc.)
